newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas continues retreat on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas continues retreat on mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices fell by more than 20 cents Monday as above-normal temperatures were expected to blanket more than half the U.S. through early next week, industry sources said.
Prices on the Gulf Coast pipes lost more than 30 cents to the low-$3.30s as milder weather was forecast to arrive to the Northeast on Wednesday.
The National Weather Service said from December 12 through December 17, temperatures would likely be above-normal over more than half of the U.S.
Extensive outages in the Northeast prevented the New York city-gate market from falling as sharply. Traders reported closing most deals in the low-to-mid $4.20s, down more than 10 cents from Friday.
PECO Energy's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear power unit in Pottstown, Pa., was shut late Friday due to an oil leak, but the company could not yet comment on a restart date.

Also, Northeast Utilities reported earlier Monday that about 162,000 electricity customers in Connecticut, New Hampshire and western Massachusetts were still without power after heavy, wet snow damaged power lines and transformers this weekend.
Temperatures in the Northeast are forecast to climb to about three to eight degrees Fahrenheit above-normal Wednesday through next Tuesday.
In the Midcontinent, where above-normal temperatures have also taken their toll on heating demand, prices dropped into the $3.23-3.28 range, down about 25 cents on the day.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were down about 20 cents to about $3.30.
Waha prices also slipped by about 20 cents to the low-$3.30s.
At the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the mid-$3.40s to mid-$3.50s, down an average of 15-20 cents.
Warmer, drier weather is forecast for most of the western U.S. over the next week.
